raw_segments.text: Macbeth, we have scorched the snake, not killed it. She'll close and be herself, whilst our
poor malice remains in danger of her former tooth. But let the frame of things disjoint,
both the worlds suffer, ere we will eat our meal in fear, and sleep in the affliction
of these terrible dreams that shake us nightly. Better be with the dead, whom we, to gain
our peace, have sent to peace, than on the torture of the mind to lie in restless ecstasy.
Duncan is in his grave. After life's fitful fever, he sleeps well. Treason has done his worst.
Nor steel, nor poison, malice, domestic, foreign levy. Nothing can touch him further.
